t: i; On Knowing God and Desecrating God's Name – x; On Shame and Arrogance

items.n: i; On Knowing God and Desecrating God's Name:1
items.e: Due to the excellence of this trait, it surpasses all other virtues, and whoever attains this level of virtue will find it easy to ascend to all other spiritual and physical virtues, one level after another. Therefore, I have prioritized it above all other virtues included in this book and have combined with this trait matters that are fundamental pillars of faith and the roots of religion, upon which the Torah stands, since they also bring man to knowledge and recognition of his Creator.
items.h: i; On Knowing God and Desecrating God's Name

items.n: i; On Knowing God and Desecrating God's Name:2
items.e: And we also need to understand and know that the Creator, may He be blessed, does not have a body nor physicality, an image, or any appearance, as it is stated, you heard the sound of words but perceived no image; nothing but a voice (Deuteronomy 4:12). And it states, To whom, then, can you liken God, what form compare to Him (Isaiah 40:18). And it likewise states, "To whom, then, can you liken Me, to whom can I be compared," says the Holy One (Isaiah 40:25). And even though we have found many verses in which physical words are written about the Creator, may He be blessed — such as the matter that is stated, The eyes of the Lord are everywhere (Proverbs 15:3); My own hand founded the earth (Isaiah 48:13); under His feet there was the likeness of a pavement of sapphire (Exodus 24:10); written with the finger of God (Exodus 24:10); and many verses like these — they were only written to make people understand what they are able to understand. And about what is similar to this, the sages, may their memory be blessed, have said, "The Torah speaks in the language of people." So it is all appellations and metaphors regarding the Creator. But the central truth is that He is without a body or physical image. And we have been much warned in the Torah to distance ourselves from it, from physicalizing, like the matter that is stated, [So you are to take exceeding care for your selves], for you did not see any image (Deuteronomy 4:15).

items.n: i; On Knowing God and Desecrating God's Name:3

items.e: The Second Virtue: The Virtue of Love of God, and Included in It the Love of One’s Fellow

My children, come and I will teach you the virtue of love of the Creator. My children, know that the virtue of loving the Creator, blessed be He, is a very great and exalted virtue. Anyone who serves the Creator out of love is called His beloved. Thus we find regarding our forefather Abraham, peace be upon him, that he served the Creator out of love and was called His beloved, as it is said: “The seed of Abraham, My beloved.” And from where do we know that Abraham our father served the Creator out of love? As it is said: “And Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey.” Did Abraham our father not have servants and members of his household who could saddle the donkey for him? From here the Sages said that love disrupts the ordinary order. Because he wished to serve his Creator with love, he himself prepared the donkey and did not command one of his household to prepare it. The virtue of this quality is found among the righteous who are known and famous for piety and abstinence. They serve their Creator out of love, not in order to receive reward or good recompense from Him. Nor do they separate themselves from sin out of fear of punishment or calamity. Rather, everything is done out of love for the Creator and in order to fulfill His commandments, like a servant who accepts the command and decree of his master. As our Sages of blessed memory said: “Do not be like servants who serve the master on condition of receiving reward.” Rather, be like servants who serve the master without expecting reward. For one who serves his master out of love is not like one who serves out of fear. When someone serves out of fear, if his master burdens him he abandons him and leaves. But one who serves out of love does not do so. For you will not find love where there is fear, nor fear where there is love, except with regard to the Holy One, blessed be He. As the Sages said: Serve out of love and serve out of fear. Serve out of love, so that if you come to hate, the lover will not hate. Serve out of fear, so that if you come to rebel, the one who fears will not rebel. Thus Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, warns Israel: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.” Anyone who serves out of love does not lose his reward, as it is said: “Showing kindness to thousands of those who love Me and keep My commandments.” Our Sages said: “You shall love the Lord your God”, with both your inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination. “With all your heart”, your heart should not be divided within you about whether to serve the Creator or not. “With all your soul”, even if He takes your life, as it is said: “For Your sake we are killed all day long.” The Sages said: Is it possible for a person to be killed every day? Rather, love Him until the exhaustion of the soul. So we find with Rabbi Akiva, when they combed his flesh with iron combs and weighed his flesh in the market. At that time it was the time of the recitation of the Shema, and he accepted upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven in order to fulfill “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,” even if He takes your life. And his soul departed on the word “One.” They also said: “With all your soul”, with every soul that He created within you. For with every breath that a person takes he must praise his Creator, as it is said: “Let every soul praise the Lord.” That is, with every breath. “With all your might”, with all your wealth. Our Sages said: If it had said “with all your soul,” why say “with all your might”? And if it had said “with all your might,” why say “with all your soul”? Because there are people whose body is more precious to them than their wealth, therefore it says “with all your soul.” And there are people whose wealth is more precious to them than their body, therefore it says “with all your might.” A parable: of a beloved servant of a king who honored the king with a gift. As long as he honors him with something dear to him, it is most pleasing to him. But if he honors him with something that is not dear to him, it brings him no satisfaction. Another explanation of “with all your might”: with every measure that He measures for you, whether a good measure or a measure of punishment, you must thank Him and bless Him greatly. As David, peace be upon him, said: “I will lift the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord. I found trouble and sorrow, and I called upon the name of the Lord.” Likewise it says: “I will sing of kindness and justice.” Meaning: if the Holy One, blessed be He, does kindness with me, I will sing and bless Him; and if He does justice with me, I will also sing and bless Him. Our Sages said: A person must bless for the bad, “Blessed is the True Judge”, just as he blesses for the good, “Blessed is the Good and the Beneficent.” Everything should be accepted from the Creator with love, joy, and a good heart, as it is said: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.” And it also says: “But You are exalted forever, O Lord.” Forever Your hand is supreme, as it is said: “The Lord gave and the Lord took away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Whether He gives or whether He takes, blessed be the name of the Lord.

My children, be careful regarding the love of the Creator, blessed be He. For anyone who loves God with all his heart, whose soul longs for Him and constantly yearns for His love, is the one who truly knows Him and clings to His ways, as it is said: “You shall love the Lord your God,” and immediately afterward it says: “And these words that I command you today shall be upon your heart.” Meaning that when a person is attached and bound in love of the Creator, His commandments will always be engraved upon his heart. You should know, my children, how a person can come to love his Creator. First, you must reflect upon the many kindnesses that the Creator has bestowed upon you. Through this you will be compelled to attach yourselves to His love and to love Him with a powerful love, especially considering that He is the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. Furthermore, my children, you must reject this world and abandon bodily pleasures for the sake of love of the Creator, and despise everything you might otherwise love, so that no cause should arise that might lead you to break your love for God. Your mouths and your hearts should be united in His love, and all your deeds, in action, in speech, when you sit in your house, when you walk on the road, and in all matters of business, your intention in all of them should be to remember His love. In this way you will establish the love of God in your hearts and love Him with a powerful love that will never depart from you. Therefore, my children, you must correct all your faults and straighten all your affairs so that everything you do will be for the love of the Creator, not in order to show people that you are pious or God-fearing, not so that people will honor you, and not so that you will rise to some position in this world. As our Sages of blessed memory said: a person should not say, “I am studying Torah so that I will become wealthy,” or “so that I will be called Rabbi,” or “so that I will receive reward in the World to Come.” Rather, as it says: “To love the Lord.” Everything you do should be done only out of love. They also said: “Happy is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in His commandments”, in the commandments themselves, and not in the reward for the commandments. They also said: Perform deeds for their own sake, and speak words of Torah for their own sake. Do not make them a crown with which to glorify yourselves, nor a tool with which to earn a livelihood.

My children, be careful regarding the love of the Creator, blessed be He. For anyone who loves God with all his heart, whose soul longs for Him and constantly yearns for His love, is the one who truly knows Him and clings to His ways, as it is said, “You shall love the Lord your God,” and immediately following it, “And these words which I command you today shall be upon your heart.” That is to say, when a person is attached and bound in the love of the Creator, His commandments will always be engraved upon his heart. You should know, my children, how a person comes to love his Creator. First, you must reflect upon the many kindnesses that the Creator has bestowed upon you. Through this you will be compelled to attach yourselves to His love and to love Him with a powerful love, especially considering that He is the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. Furthermore, my children, you must despise this world and abandon bodily pleasures for the sake of the love of the Creator, and reject everything you might otherwise love so that no cause will arise that might cause you to break your love of God. Your mouths and your hearts should be united in His love, and all your deeds, in action, in speech, in sitting in your home, in walking along the road, and in all matters of business, your intention in all of them should be to remember His love. In this way you will establish the love of God within your hearts and love Him with a strong love that will never depart from you. Therefore, my children, you must correct all your faults and straighten all your affairs so that everything will be done for the love of the Creator, not in order to show people that you are pious and God-fearing, not so that people will honor you, and not so that you will be elevated to any position in this world. As our Sages said, a person should not say, “I am studying Torah so that I will become wealthy,” or “so that I will be called Rabbi,” or “so that I will receive a reward in the World to Come.” Rather, as it is written, “to love the Lord.” Everything you do should be done only out of love. They also said, “Happy is the man who fears the Lord; he greatly delights in His commandments,” meaning in the commandments themselves and not in their reward. They also said, perform deeds for their own sake and speak words of Torah for their own sake, and do not make them a crown to glorify yourselves nor a tool with which to earn your livelihood.

My children, love your wives as your own bodies, just as you wish them to love you, and honor them with clothing and ornaments even more than yourselves, as it is said: “A loving doe, a graceful deer; let her breasts satisfy you at all times, and always be intoxicated with her love.” Love also your children, your brothers, and your relatives, as it is said: “Do not hide yourself from your own flesh.” Love also your friends and your good neighbors, for sometimes they may help you more than your relatives, as it is said: “A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.” And it also says: “A close neighbor is better than a distant brother.”

My children, conduct yourselves with every person according to this teaching, for through it the love of people toward you will increase. As one wise man said, whoever wishes to be loved by people should behave toward them with good character. Just as harm brings a person to hatred, so benefit brings a person to love. Love the Torah and the commandments, as it is said: “How I love Your Torah; it is my meditation all day.” Love also those who are engaged in Torah and commandments, as it is said: “I love those who love Me, and those who seek Me will find Me.” The word is written “those who love her,” which according to the tradition refers to those who love the Torah and the commandments. It was also said that anyone who interacts with people and conducts business with them in faithfulness, honesty, love, and peace plants love in the hearts of others and obtains from them whatever he desires. It is told that a man once asked a friend who loved him greatly, “Why do you love me, since I am neither your relative nor your neighbor?” He answered, “Because I see you interacting with every person and you do not despise those who are lower than you in rank or in years. When I saw you conduct yourself with humility and good character, your love became bound in my heart and I loved you with a complete love.” It was also said that nothing turns an enemy into a friend like humility and good character. Therefore, my children, be careful in the love of the Creator and in the love of all people. Seek to please every person with pleasant and agreeable words and with good deeds so that people will love you and not hate you, as our Sages said, “Your deeds will draw you near and your deeds will distance you.” If people hate you, it is certain that you will come to hate them, and regarding this the Torah warned, “You shall not hate your brother in your heart.” One wise man said that whoever sows hatred will reap regret, and another said that there is no evil like the hatred of people, whether the hatred of the honorable or the lowly, for sometimes a great man may be choked by a small fly. If you have enemies and you seek revenge against them, strive instead to add greater virtues to your good qualities, as one wise man answered when asked how a person should take revenge upon his enemy, that he should increase his own virtue. Aristotle also instructed Alexander the king that the most important thing he commands and warns him about is not to hate any person in the world whom God created, for the beginning of wisdom after recognizing the truth of God is the love of all people, both good and bad. May God grant us success in His love so that we may merit to inherit the days of the Messiah and the life of the World to Come, as it is said: “That I may cause those who love Me to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasuries.”

My children, come and I will teach you the virtue of modesty. My children, you should know that the virtue of modesty is from the most important and pedigreed traits. As it one of the three traits that the Holy One, blessed be He, seeks from the Jewish people, as it is stated: And what does the Lord require of you, etc. and to walk modestly with your God (Micah 6:8). And not only that, but it protects a person from the evil eye, and saves him from sins and transgressions. For such do we find with the righteous Joseph, that because he acted modestly, he was saved from his mistress, the wife of Potiphar, and did stumble because of her. It is like the matter is stated: and his master's wife lifted her eyes, etc. . She lifted her eyes in order to gaze at him, but he did not lift his eyes to gaze at her. Accordingly did the sages, may their memory be blessed, say in the recountings (Bereishit Rabbah 87:10), that she placed an iron bar beneath his neck until he would direct his glance toward her and look at her. Nevertheless, he would not look at her. As it is stated: They tortured his legs with chains; his body was placed in iron (Psalms 105:18). And we found that a certain matron asked Rabbi Yose: She said to him, "Is it possible that Joseph was seventeen years old, standing in vigor, and he would not have done that thing?" He brought out the book of Genesis in front of them. He began to read the story of Reuben, and of Judah and Tamar. He said to her, "If Scripture did not cover for these, who were older and under their father's authority, all the more so would it be for this one who was younger and under his own authority."

My children, come and I will teach you about the virtue of **shame (bushah)**. Know, my children, that the quality of modest shame is an exceedingly important virtue. Anyone who possesses a sense of shame is saved from sins and transgressions. As it is written: *"Moses answered the people, “Be not afraid; for God has come only in order to test you, and in order that the fear of God may be ever with you, so that you do not go astray."* (Shemot 20:17). Our Sages said: *“ that the fear of God may be ever with you”*, this refers to **shame**. *“So that you do not go astray”*, this teaches that **shame leads a person to fear of sin**. From here they said: **A good sign for a person is that he is bashful.** And one wise man said: **A sign of worthy children is the modest shame that appears upon their faces.*

And this virtue is found only among the pious and those who fear sin, as our Sages said: “Anyone who feels shame does not quickly come to sin.” And whoever has no sense of shame, it is known that his ancestors did not stand at Mount Sinai.

My children, come and see how great the virtue of shame is before the Omnipresent. Even if a person has committed many transgressions, if he feels ashamed of them and does not repeat them, the Holy One, blessed be He, forgives him for all his sins, as it is said: “Thus you shall remember and feel shame, and you shall be too abashed to open your mouth again, when I have forgiven you for all that you did, declares the Sovereign GOD.” (Yechezkel 16:63). We also find this with King Shaul. When Shmuel was brought up through the woman with the familiar spirit, he said to Saul: “Why have you disturbed me to bring me up?” Shaul replied: “I am greatly distressed; the Philistines are fighting against me, and God has turned away from me and no longer answers me, neither through the prophets nor through dreams, so I have called you to tell me what I should do.” However, Shaul was ashamed to mention the Urim and Tumim because he had killed the priests of Nov, and the Holy One, blessed be He, forgave him, as it is said: “Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me,” meaning with me in my portion. Our Sages said that anyone who commits a sin and then regrets it is forgiven immediately, as it is written: “And I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the adulterers, the sorcerers, those who swear falsely, those who oppress the hired worker in his wages, the widow, the orphan, and those who turn aside the stranger and do not fear Me,” implying that if they do fear Me they are forgiven. And so it says: “He who confesses and abandons his sins will obtain mercy.” One wise man said: Be careful with the trait of shame, for shame is visible upon the face of a noble person. Another said: He whom the Creator clothes with the cloak of shame, his faults will be hidden from people.

Great is the trait of shame, for through it a person merits good deeds, and not only that, but he also merits the Garden of Eden, as our Sages said: the brazen-faced are destined for Gehinnom, and the bashful for the Garden of Eden. One wise man said that shame and faith cling together; when one departs, the other departs as well. What is shame? It is that a person should feel ashamed of himself and of his deeds when he is alone with himself, and he should also feel ashamed before other people. He should be modest in all his ways and in all his matters, examining them carefully so that no blemish or disgraceful thing will arise in them, so that if others see or hear of them he will not be put to shame. He should reflect at the beginning of a matter before doing it, so that he will strive to act in a way that will not bring him to shame. He should be modest in eating and drinking so that he will not become disgraceful, degraded, or ashamed before others. He should distance himself from ugliness and from anything similar to it. In summary, he should feel shame before the Creator, and then the virtue of the trait of shame will be complete within him, as one wise man said: when you do something inside your house, be ashamed before the members of your household; when you do something in the marketplace, be ashamed before people; if not, then be ashamed before yourself; and if you are not ashamed before yourself, then be ashamed before your soul; and if you are not ashamed before your soul, then be ashamed before the Creator who sees you.

My children, be careful with the trait of shame, for when a person is ashamed before people he becomes careful to avoid disgraceful and ugly things and does not stumble in them. All the more so if he is ashamed before the Creator, he will not stumble in sin and transgression. Anyone who has no sense of shame has already come to regard the Torah as something permitted in his eyes, as one wise man said: the final teaching we received from the words of prophecy is that when you are not ashamed, you will do whatever you wish. It is also said that suspicion will not reach the bashful person just as the sound of theft and robbery will not reach the trustworthy one. They asked a wise man, “What is shame?” He answered, “Intellect.” They said to him, “And what is intellect?” He answered, “Shame.” Another said: shame is the path to long life. And another said: the life of a person is sustained first by faith and fear of God for many days, and afterwards his life continues through the traits of shame, humility, and lowliness.

My children, be careful not to shame your fellow, even when you are alone with him, and all the more so not to shame him in public, for it is one of the most serious transgressions in the Torah. Our Sages said: anyone who whitens the face of his fellow in public is as if he has shed blood, for we see that the redness leaves his face and paleness comes. They also said that anyone who shames his fellow will in the end be shamed himself. Not only that, but the ministering angels push him away and display his disgrace before all who come into the world. They further said that all who descend to Gehinnom descend and later rise again, except for three who descend and do not rise: one who has relations with a married woman, one who gives his fellow a degrading nickname, and one who shames his fellow in public. Know that because they shamed Bar Kamtza in public, the Holy One, blessed be He, allowed the destruction of the Temple.

Even though I have warned you about the virtue of shame, I also warn you that if you have made a mistake in any matter, do not be ashamed to return and admit the truth. For anyone who is ashamed to return and acknowledge the truth is certainly called brazen-faced. And if you have sinned, whether unintentionally or intentionally, in any matter of the Torah and its commandments, do not be ashamed to confess it before the Creator. Likewise, when you are in doubt about something from the words of the Torah, or from the received tradition, or about any commandment, do not be ashamed to ask about it, even from someone lesser than you in rank or in years. Do not be ashamed to say about something you do not know, “We do not know.” And about something you have not heard, say, “We have not heard.” Or if you heard it but do not remember, say, “We heard it but we forgot.” For even Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, admitted and was not ashamed to say, “I have not heard,” as it is said: “And Moses heard, and it was good in his eyes.” Our Sages said: the bashful person does not learn, and the impatient person does not teach. And it was taught in the school of Elijah: a person should ask about a verse even if everyone laughs at him, and about a halachah even if everyone laughs at him. A person should bring himself into the body of the Torah even if he is not proficient in halachah at all, as it is said: “If you have acted foolishly in exalting yourself, or if you have planned evil, put your hand over your mouth.” Likewise, do not be ashamed to warn a person and guide him in a good path, for refraining from doing so is not the way of people who are complete in their character traits, and that kind of shame is worse than brazenness. Therefore, my children, be careful with the trait of shame, so that the fear of God will always be upon your faces and you will not sin. And may our God, in His mercy, grant us success in it.

And after we have come this far in speaking about the praise of the virtue of shame and those who possess it, we will now speak about the disgrace of brazenness and those who possess it, in order to guide you in the trait of shame, with the help of the Almighty.

My children, know that the trait of brazenness is a quality greatly despised in the eyes of the Omnipresent, because it is like a branch of idolatry. Not only that, but because of brazen people the heavens are restrained from sending dew and rain, as it is said: “Therefore the showers have been withheld, and the latter rain has not come; yet you had the forehead of a harlot, you refused to be ashamed.” (Yirmiahu 3:3). Our Sages also said that Jerusalem was destroyed only because they had no sense of shame toward one another, as it is said: “Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? No, they were not ashamed at all, nor did they know how to blush.” (Yirmiahu 6:15). This disgraceful trait is not found among the pious and people of good deeds, but rather among the wicked, as it is said about them: “They have made their faces harder than rock.” (Yirmiahu 5:3). Our Sages further said that anyone who possesses brazenness may be called a wicked person to his face, as it is said: “A wicked man hardens his face.” (Mishlei 21:29). Anyone who has brazenness will in the end fall and be broken. And it was taught in the school of Elijah that the intimidating, the arrogant boasters, the brazen-faced, and the strong-armed, about them the verse says: “For the arms of the wicked shall be broken.”

My children, come and see how severe the trait of brazenness is, for once a person has brazenness he comes to wickedness, as it is said: “A wicked man hardens his face.” Not only that, but anyone who has brazenness is known to have stumbled in sin, as it is said: “You had the forehead of a harlot.” It does not say “you will have,” but “you had already.” Our Sages said in the Aggadah that four are called wicked: one who raises his hand against his fellow to strike him, even if he did not strike him, is called wicked, as it is said: “And he said to the wicked one, ‘Why will you strike your fellow?’” It does not say “why did you strike,” but “why will you strike.” One who borrows and does not repay, as it is said: “The wicked borrows and does not repay.” One who has brazenness, as it is said: “A wicked man hardens his face.” And one who is a man of dispute, as it is said: “Depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men.” Both of these traits were found in Dathan and Abiram, brazenness and dispute. There is no brazen person who does not have some flaw in his lineage, as our Sages said: a brazen person, Rabbi Eliezer says he is a mamzer; Rabbi Yehoshua says he is the son of a woman in a state of niddah; Rabbi Akiva says he is both a mamzer and the son of a niddah. What is brazenness? One who commits a sin in front of other people and is not ashamed is called brazen-faced. One who commits a sin and repeats it, and walks with an upright posture and a brazen forehead without shame, is like an idol worshipper, as it is said: “They were ashamed because they committed abomination, yet they were not ashamed.” The end of brazenness is dispute, and after dispute comes regret. It is also said that brazenness is a great sickness, and its cure is found in a person equally bold in opposing it.

However, to stand with boldness against the wicked and those who abandon the Torah in order to discipline them and rebuke them is very good, as it is said: “Behold, I have made you a fortified city, an iron pillar, and a wall of bronze.” For this reason Solomon commanded and said: “Answer a fool according to his folly.” Therefore, my children, be careful of this disgraceful trait and distance it from yourselves, and do not make use of it so that it will not overcome you, for anyone who possesses this disgraceful trait will find that people distance themselves from him and turn away from him. May God save us from disgraceful and base traits and raise us to the highest virtues through His mercy and abundant kindness. Amen.
